ideas.title: Extend Export Panel to Multiple Image Formats
ideas.description: Add JPEG, WebP, and SVG export options to the ExportPanel component. The current implementation only exports PNG format, but the canvas infrastructure supports other formats. Users would benefit from choosing quality/size tradeoffs with JPEG, modern WebP compression, or vector SVG for designs without photos.
ideas.rationale: The ExportPanel.tsx already has the export infrastructure with canvas.generateStageImage(). The pattern for adding format selection exists in CanvasFormatSelector.tsx. The canvas ref architecture supports multiple output formats via the toDataURL method.
ideas.implementation_approach: Add a format selector dropdown (reuse pattern from CanvasFormatSelector) with options PNG/JPEG/WebP. Modify handleDownload to pass format and quality parameters to canvas.toDataURL(). Add quality slider for JPEG/WebP (0-100). Update filename extension based on selected format.

ideas.title: Extend Keyboard Shortcuts for Canvas Operations
ideas.description: Add keyboard shortcuts for common canvas operations: Tab navigation (Ctrl+1/2/3), duplicate element (Ctrl+D), delete element (Delete/Backspace), zoom in/out (Ctrl++/-), toggle safe zones (Ctrl+;), and quick export (Ctrl+E). The shortcut infrastructure is robust but currently underutilized.
ideas.rationale: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts provides excellent infrastructure with modifier key support, input field detection, and formatted display. getDefaultShortcuts already defines 7 shortcuts but many common canvas operations are missing. The pattern is proven and tested.
ideas.implementation_approach: Extend getDefaultShortcuts handlers object to include new callbacks: onDuplicate, onDelete, onZoomIn, onZoomOut, onToggleSafeZones, onQuickExport, onTabStudio, onTabGallery, onTabBrainstorm. Add corresponding shortcut definitions following existing pattern. Update KeyboardShortcutsPanel to display all shortcuts.

ideas.title: Add Model Usage Analytics Hook and Display
ideas.description: Create a useModelUsage hook that aggregates performance metrics from AIContext to show model usage statistics: calls per model, average latency, total cost, and success rates. Display in a new ModelUsagePanel or extend PerformanceMetricsPanel.
ideas.rationale: AIContext already tracks performanceMetrics in localStorage with model, latency, and success data. modelRouter.ts has comprehensive model metadata including costs. The useMetrics hook pattern from admin features shows how to aggregate and display metrics with period filtering.
ideas.implementation_approach: Create useModelUsage hook that reads performanceMetrics from AIContext, groups by model/provider, calculates aggregates (count, avgLatency, totalCost, successRate). Use same return pattern as useMetrics (data, isLoading, period, setPeriod). Extend PerformanceMetricsPanel or create ModelUsagePanel to visualize with bar charts for model comparison.

ideas.title: Add Error Rate Tracking to Error Handler
ideas.description: Extend errorHandler.ts to track error rates by type and endpoint, storing in localStorage for display in admin dashboard. Add useErrorMetrics hook following the established metrics hook pattern to surface error trends.
ideas.rationale: errorHandler.ts already classifies errors into types (network, cors, timeout, api, unknown) with the classifyError function. The admin dashboard has useMetrics, useCostBreakdown, useTraces patterns for metrics aggregation. Missing link is persisting and aggregating client-side error data.
ideas.implementation_approach: Add trackError function to errorHandler.ts that stores {timestamp, type, endpoint, message} to localStorage (limit to last 1000 entries). Create useErrorMetrics hook following useMetrics pattern - aggregates errors by type and time period, calculates rates. Return {errorsByType, errorRate, recentErrors, period}.

ideas.title: Add Agent Task Routing Suggestions
ideas.description: Extend the agent registry to suggest the best agent for user queries based on keywords and intent analysis. Add a getAgentSuggestions function that analyzes input text and returns ranked agent recommendations with confidence scores.
ideas.rationale: The agent registry (registry.ts) has getDefaultAgentForTask with a simple keyword-to-agent map. Each agent has detailed capabilities, tools, and systemPrompt. The model router shows pattern for intelligent selection with selectModelForTask. Can apply same pattern to agent selection.
ideas.implementation_approach: Add getAgentSuggestions(query: string): AgentSuggestion[] to registry.ts. Analyze query for keywords matching agent capabilities/tools. Score each agent based on capability matches, return top 3 with confidence. Add UI hint in ChatInterface showing suggested agent when query is typed. Follow model router pattern for fallback selection.

ideas.title: Add Modal Accessibility with Focus Trap
ideas.description: Enhance AuthModal and other modal dialogs with proper ARIA attributes (role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby), focus trapping to keep keyboard focus within the modal, and ESC key dismissal. Currently the AuthModal lacks these critical accessibility features.
ideas.rationale: Modal dialogs without focus traps allow users to tab out of the modal to background content, creating confusion for keyboard and screen reader users. Proper ARIA attributes ensure assistive technologies announce the modal correctly. This is a WCAG 2.1 Level A requirement.
ideas.current_state: AuthModal at line 152 opens as a fixed overlay but lacks role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby for the heading. Close button at line 155 lacks aria-label. No focus trap implementation exists - users can tab to background elements. ESC key does not dismiss the modal.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' to modal container div. 2. Add unique id to modal heading (e.g., id='auth-modal-title') and reference it with aria-labelledby on the container. 3. Add aria-label='Close dialog' to close button. 4. Implement focus trap using a useEffect hook that captures Tab key events and cycles focus within modal elements. 5. Add keydown listener for ESC key to call onClose. 6. Move initial focus to first focusable element on open. 7. Restore focus to trigger element on close.
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard-only users can navigate modals properly without accidentally interacting with background content. Screen reader users hear proper modal announcements. All users can dismiss modals quickly with ESC key.

ideas.title: Replace Bouncing Notification with Smooth Toast
ideas.description: Replace the current notification toast that uses 'animate-bounce' animation with a more subtle slide-in animation, auto-dismiss timer, and stacking support for multiple notifications. The bounce animation is visually distracting and does not communicate urgency appropriately.
ideas.rationale: The bounce animation (line 461 in App.tsx) creates visual noise and can be disorienting, especially for users with vestibular disorders. Modern toast notifications use smooth entrance animations and auto-dismiss after a configurable duration. This improves perceived polish and reduces cognitive load.
ideas.current_state: Notification toast at lines 459-473 in App.tsx uses 'animate-bounce' class and requires manual dismissal via close button. It appears at 'fixed top-16 md:top-20' position. No auto-dismiss timer exists. Multiple notifications would overlap.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Replace 'animate-bounce' with custom CSS animation: 'animate-in slide-in-from-top-2 duration-300'. 2. Add auto-dismiss with configurable timeout (default 5 seconds for info, 8 seconds for warnings). 3. Implement notification queue/stack system that shows up to 3 notifications with vertical stacking. 4. Add aria-live='polite' for info and aria-live='assertive' for warnings. 5. Add subtle exit animation 'animate-out slide-out-to-top duration-200' before removal. 6. Consider extracting to a reusable <Toast> or <Notification> component.
ideas.user_benefit: Users experience smoother, less intrusive notifications. Auto-dismiss means users don't need to manually close routine messages. Reduced motion for users who prefer it. Screen readers properly announce notifications.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Navigation to Profile Dropdown Menu
ideas.description: Enhance the profile dropdown menu in Header.tsx with proper ARIA menu pattern including role='menu', role='menuitem', aria-expanded, keyboard navigation with arrow keys, and focus management.
ideas.rationale: The profile dropdown (lines 169-208 in Header.tsx) lacks standard dropdown menu accessibility. Users cannot navigate menu items with arrow keys, and the menu lacks proper ARIA roles for screen readers. This creates a barrier for keyboard-only and screen reader users.
ideas.current_state: Profile button at line 160 toggles showProfileMenu state but lacks aria-expanded attribute. Dropdown container at line 169 lacks role='menu'. Individual buttons within lack role='menuitem'. No keyboard navigation - users cannot use arrow keys to navigate items. Focus does not move to first menu item when opened.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add aria-expanded={showProfileMenu} and aria-haspopup='menu' to profile button. 2. Add role='menu' and aria-label='User menu' to dropdown container. 3. Add role='menuitem' and tabIndex={-1} to each menu item button. 4. Implement useEffect with keydown listener for ArrowDown/ArrowUp navigation between items. 5. Move focus to first menu item when dropdown opens. 6. Close menu and return focus to trigger on ESC. 7. Close menu when clicking outside. 8. Apply same pattern to model selector dropdown in GenerativeSidebar.tsx (line 157).
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard users can navigate dropdown menus efficiently with arrow keys. Screen readers properly announce menu structure and current focus. Menu behavior matches user expectations from native OS menus.

ideas.title: Add Skeleton Loading States for Gallery and Components
ideas.description: Replace simple spinner loading indicators with content-shaped skeleton screens for ImageGallery, tab content areas, and Suspense fallbacks. Skeleton screens provide better perceived performance by showing the approximate layout of content while loading.
ideas.rationale: Current loading states (e.g., lines 510, 517, 526, 535 in App.tsx) use simple spinning circles. Research shows skeleton screens reduce perceived load time by up to 50% because users see a preview of incoming content structure. This is especially important for image-heavy content like the gallery.
ideas.current_state: Suspense fallbacks at lines 510, 517, 526, 535 in App.tsx show generic spinning circle with 'border-b-2 border-[color]' pattern. ImageGallery loading state (if any) likely shows spinner. Users see blank space with spinner, providing no information about what will appear.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Create reusable <SkeletonCard> component with shimmer animation ('animate-pulse bg-zinc-800 rounded-xl'). 2. Create <GallerySkeleton> showing grid of 6-8 card placeholders matching gallery card dimensions. 3. Create <StudioSkeleton> showing canvas area + sidebar outlines. 4. Create <ChatSkeleton> showing message bubble outlines. 5. Replace Suspense fallback spinners with appropriate skeleton components. 6. Use consistent shimmer animation: 'animate-pulse' with subtle gradient overlay. 7. Match skeleton shapes to actual component layouts for seamless transition.
ideas.user_benefit: Users perceive faster load times and understand what content is coming. Reduced cognitive load from layout shifts when content appears. Professional, polished feel that matches modern web applications.

ideas.title: Improve Voice Agent Connection Feedback
ideas.description: Enhance the voice agent toggle button and LiveActionPanel with better visual and potentially haptic feedback during connection states. Add intermediate 'connecting' state, connection error recovery UI, and clearer status indicators.
ideas.rationale: The voice agent button (lines 107-118 in Header.tsx) only shows two states: active (green pulse) and inactive. Users don't see feedback during the connection process or understand why connection might fail. LiveActionPanel could benefit from clearer status transitions.
ideas.current_state: Voice button at lines 107-118 shows binary state with immediate toggle. No 'connecting' animation during the async connect() call (lines 59-67 in App.tsx). Connection errors show generic notification. LiveActionPanel status bar (lines 85-100) shows connected/not connected but no intermediate states.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add 'isConnecting' state to track connection in progress. 2. Show intermediate button state during connection: amber/yellow color with spinning icon instead of mic icon. 3. Add aria-label that reflects current state: 'Connecting to voice agent...' during connection. 4. Show connection progress indicator in LiveActionPanel status bar. 5. Add haptic feedback on mobile when connection succeeds (navigator.vibrate([50]) if supported). 6. Show retry button in notification on connection failure instead of generic message. 7. Add subtle audio feedback (short tone) on successful connection. 8. Update button title/tooltip dynamically: 'Connecting...' / 'Connected - Click to disconnect' / 'Click to connect voice agent'.
ideas.user_benefit: Users clearly understand the current state of voice agent connection. Intermediate feedback reduces uncertainty during async operations. Haptic/audio feedback confirms successful actions for users who may not be looking at the screen. Clear recovery path from errors.

ideas.title: Upgrade vulnerable npm dependencies with known CVEs
ideas.description: npm audit reveals 4 vulnerabilities in dependencies: esbuild (<=0.24.2) has a moderate severity request handling issue, path-to-regexp (4.0.0-6.2.2) has a HIGH severity ReDoS vulnerability enabling denial of service via backtracking regex, and undici (<=5.28.5) has two moderate vulnerabilities including insufficient random values and certificate handling issues.
ideas.rationale: High severity vulnerabilities like ReDoS in path-to-regexp can be exploited by attackers to cause denial of service by crafting malicious URLs. The undici vulnerabilities could compromise secure communications.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-1333: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity, CWE-330: Insufficient Random Values
ideas.currentRisk: ReDoS attacks on routing, potential DoS via path-to-regexp. Certificate validation issues in undici could allow MITM attacks.
ideas.remediation: Run `npm audit fix --force` to upgrade @vercel/node to version 2.3.0 (breaking change). Alternatively, upgrade individual packages: path-to-regexp to >=6.3.0, undici to >=5.28.6, esbuild to >=0.25.0. Review breaking changes in @vercel/node before upgrading.

ideas.title: Hash password reset tokens before database storage
ideas.description: In server/src/routes/auth.ts line 216, password reset tokens are stored in plaintext in the database with an explicit comment noting 'Storing plain token for MVP simplicity, usually hash it'. This leaves reset tokens vulnerable if the database is compromised.
ideas.rationale: Password reset tokens grant full account takeover capability. If an attacker gains read access to the database (via SQL injection, backup leak, or insider threat), they can use any unexpired reset token to take over accounts. Hashing tokens with SHA-256 prevents this attack vector.
ideas.currentRisk: Database breach exposes all active password reset tokens, enabling mass account takeover
ideas.remediation: 1. Hash the reset token with SHA-256 before storing: `const tokenHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex')`. 2. Send the unhashed token to user via email. 3. When validating, hash the submitted token and compare to stored hash. 4. Rename 'tokenHash' column if needed for clarity (it's currently storing plaintext despite the name).

ideas.title: Implement CSRF protection for state-changing endpoints
ideas.description: The application lacks CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) protection. State-changing endpoints like /api/auth/login, /api/user/api-keys, and /api/designs rely solely on session cookies for authentication. An attacker could trick authenticated users into performing unwanted actions by embedding requests in malicious websites.
ideas.rationale: Without CSRF tokens, any website can submit forms to the application on behalf of authenticated users. This is particularly dangerous for API key management and account operations. The SameSite cookie attribute provides partial protection but is insufficient for older browsers and certain attack vectors.
ideas.currentRisk: Authenticated users visiting malicious sites could unknowingly trigger account changes, API key modifications, or design deletions
ideas.remediation: 1. Create server/src/lib/csrf.ts with token generation using crypto.randomBytes(32). 2. Set CSRF token in a double-submit cookie pattern. 3. Add CSRF middleware to validate X-CSRF-Token header on POST/PUT/DELETE requests. 4. Update frontend api.ts to include CSRF token from cookie in request headers. 5. Consider using Hono's built-in csrf middleware.

ideas.title: Remove API key access from localStorage in ModelSelector component
ideas.description: The ModelSelector component (src/components/features/ModelSelector.tsx line 29) still reads API keys directly from localStorage. While the main apiKeyStorage service has been updated to use server-side storage, this legacy pattern could lead to inconsistent behavior and expose keys to XSS attacks.
ideas.rationale: localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, making stored secrets vulnerable to XSS attacks. Although the migration to server-side storage is underway, legacy code patterns that access localStorage directly could cause confusion and security regressions. The migrateLocalStorageToNeon function in apiKeyStorage.ts also reads from localStorage for migration purposes but doesn't clear the old values.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
ideas.currentRisk: XSS vulnerability anywhere in the app could extract API keys from localStorage. Legacy code may bypass intended server-side key storage.
ideas.remediation: 1. Update ModelSelector to get API key availability status from AIContext or call getUserAPIKeys() instead of localStorage.getItem('openrouter_api_key'). 2. After successful migration, clear localStorage keys using localStorage.removeItem(). 3. Add a cleanup function in migrateLocalStorageToNeon() that removes keys after successful server storage. 4. Search codebase for all localStorage.getItem calls referencing *_api_key and update them.

ideas.title: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
ideas.description: The application has basic security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, X-Content-Type-Options) but lacks a Content Security Policy. CSP is the most effective defense against XSS attacks, controlling which sources can load scripts, styles, images, and other resources.
ideas.rationale: Without CSP, any injected script can execute and exfiltrate data. Given this app handles API keys and uses multiple AI service integrations, CSP provides critical defense-in-depth against XSS. The application already connects to known external domains (replicate.com, openrouter.ai, googleapis.com) that can be whitelisted.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
ideas.currentRisk: XSS attacks can freely execute malicious JavaScript, steal session cookies (unless HttpOnly), exfiltrate API keys from localStorage, and perform actions on behalf of users
ideas.remediation: Add CSP header in server/src/index.ts security headers middleware. Start with report-only mode: `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https://*.replicate.delivery https://*.supabase.co; connect-src 'self' https://api.replicate.com https://openrouter.ai https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com; frame-ancestors 'none';` Monitor violations before enforcing. Gradually remove 'unsafe-inline' by using nonces or hashes.

ideas.title: Add Voice Agent User Guide and Command Reference
ideas.description: The voice-powered design system (VoiceAgentContext, liveClient.ts, actionExecutor.ts) enables hands-free banner creation but has no user-facing documentation. Users cannot discover available voice commands like 'generate background', 'remove background', 'upscale image', or 'add text element'. The ActionExecutor supports 15+ tool commands but these are only documented in code comments.
ideas.rationale: Voice control is a flagship feature mentioned in README.md ('Voice-Powered Creation', 'Hands-Free Design'). Without documentation, users must guess commands or read source code. This creates a significant onboarding barrier for the primary target audience (non-technical Careersy Community members).
ideas.currentDocumentation: README mentions voice features exist but provides no command reference. ActionExecutor has inline comments describing each tool but these are not user-accessible.
ideas.proposedContent: Create docs/guides/VOICE_COMMANDS.md with: (1) Getting Started with Voice - mic setup, browser requirements (2) Full command reference table with examples ('Generate a blue tech background', 'Upscale this image to 4K') (3) Troubleshooting common issues (mic permissions, connectivity) (4) Best practices for voice prompts

ideas.title: Document React Context Architecture and Provider Hierarchy
ideas.description: The application uses 5 React contexts (AIContext, CanvasContext, AuthContext, VoiceAgentContext, plus canvas sub-contexts) but there's no documentation explaining their relationships, what state each manages, or the required provider nesting order. Developers must read App.tsx and trace imports to understand the architecture.
ideas.rationale: New contributors frequently make mistakes with context ordering or duplicate context usage. The WIKI.md architecture section shows a high-level diagram but doesn't cover the context system. This gap causes onboarding friction and bugs from incorrect context usage.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Individual context files have brief header comments. WIKI.md has architecture diagram but doesn't cover contexts. No documentation of AIContextType interface or hook usage patterns.
ideas.proposedContent: Add 'Context Architecture' section to WIKI.md explaining: (1) What each context manages (AIContext=model selection/metrics, CanvasContext=canvas state, etc.) (2) Required provider nesting order with code example (3) When to use useAI() vs useCanvas() vs useAuth() (4) Common patterns and anti-patterns

ideas.title: Create Agent System Architecture README
ideas.description: The src/services/agents/ directory contains a sophisticated multi-agent orchestration system (BaseAgent, ImageGenerationAgent, PromptEnhancementAgent, PartnerAgent, ModelRouterAgent) with excellent JSDoc on individual files, but no high-level documentation explaining how agents work together, when to use agent mode vs direct API calls, or how to create new agents.
ideas.rationale: The agent system is a key architectural pattern for the application. llm.ts has a 'useAgent' parameter but developers don't know when to use it. The BaseAgent class has extensive documentation but no guide explaining the overall system design or extension patterns.
ideas.currentDocumentation: BaseAgent.ts has excellent module-level JSDoc. Individual agents have @example blocks. No overview documentation exists. CLAUDE.md mentions agents but focuses on orchestrator agents, not application agents.
ideas.proposedContent: Create src/services/agents/README.md with: (1) Agent system overview and design philosophy (2) Agent lifecycle diagram (initialize -> execute -> shutdown) (3) When to use useAgent=true in llm.ts calls (4) How to create a new agent with code template (5) Message flow and retry logic explanation

ideas.title: Document Backend API Routes and Request/Response Schemas
ideas.description: The frontend makes calls to /api/ai/* endpoints (chat, image/generate, image/edit, image/upscale, prompt/enhance, etc.) through api.ts, but there's no documentation of the expected request payloads, response formats, error codes, or rate limiting behavior. Developers must trace code or guess API contracts.
ideas.rationale: The API layer is critical for understanding the application flow. llm.ts shows various endpoint calls but developers can't quickly reference what parameters are required or optional. This is especially problematic when debugging failed requests or adding new features.
ideas.currentDocumentation: No API documentation exists. Endpoint behavior must be inferred from llm.ts calls and server implementation. Error handling is ad-hoc.
ideas.proposedContent: Create docs/api/API_REFERENCE.md documenting: (1) Each /api/ai/* endpoint with method, path, request body schema, response schema (2) Error codes and their meanings (KEY_MISSING, RATE_LIMITED, etc.) (3) Provider-specific behavior (openrouter vs replicate vs gemini) (4) Authentication requirements (how BYOK keys are passed)

ideas.title: Add TypeScript Type System Documentation
ideas.description: Types are split across multiple files (types/ai.ts, types/database.ts, types/index.ts, types/replicate.ts, services/agents/types.ts) without documentation explaining the organization, when to import from which file, or the relationship between similar types (e.g., ModelMetadata vs AIContextType).
ideas.rationale: Developers frequently import from wrong type files or duplicate types. The split between ai.ts and agents/types.ts is confusing since both contain AI-related types. Constants.ts also exports types alongside MODELS constants. This causes inconsistent imports and confusion.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Types have inline documentation for individual interfaces but no overview of the type system organization. No guidance on where to add new types or which file to import from.
ideas.proposedContent: Create src/types/README.md explaining: (1) Type file organization (ai.ts=context types, database.ts=Supabase types, etc.) (2) Import conventions with examples (3) Type hierarchy diagram showing relationships (4) Guidelines for adding new types (5) Cross-reference with agents/types.ts vs types/ai.ts

ideas.title: Memoize getModelMetadata() to prevent expensive object recreation
ideas.description: The `getModelMetadata()` function in `modelRouter.ts` creates a new object containing 40+ model definitions on every single call. This function is called during model selection, cost estimation, and UI rendering, causing significant memory churn and CPU overhead.
ideas.rationale: Each call creates ~2KB of new objects that immediately become garbage. With frequent calls during model selection/display, this creates GC pressure and unnecessary computation. The model data is static and never changes at runtime, making it a perfect candidate for memoization.
ideas.currentMetric: ~40+ object allocations per getModelMetadata() call, potentially hundreds of calls during a session
ideas.expectedImprovement: Reduce memory allocations by 99%, eliminate redundant computation, ~50-100ms faster initial model selection
ideas.implementation:
1. Move the model metadata object to module-level const declaration
2. Export the constant directly instead of returning from function
3. Alternative: Use a lazy singleton pattern if initialization timing matters
4. Update all callsites to use the constant directly
ideas.tradeoffs: None - this is pure optimization with no behavioral changes

ideas.title: Virtualize ImageGallery grid for large collections
ideas.description: The ImageGallery component renders ALL images in the user's collection at once. For users with 50+ generated images, this causes significant DOM bloat and slow initial render times as each image card creates multiple DOM nodes.
ideas.rationale: Each image card contains 8+ DOM elements (image, overlays, buttons, badges). With 100 images, that's 800+ DOM nodes always mounted. Virtual scrolling only renders visible items plus a small buffer, typically reducing DOM nodes from 800 to ~40.
ideas.currentMetric: Full DOM render of all gallery items, ~100ms+ render time for 50+ images
ideas.expectedImprovement: Constant O(1) render time regardless of collection size, ~90% reduction in DOM nodes, smoother scrolling
ideas.implementation:
1. Install react-window or @tanstack/virtual
2. Wrap the image grid with FixedSizeGrid or VirtualGrid
3. Adjust item size calculations for responsive grid
4. Implement proper keyboard navigation for accessibility
5. Add scroll position restoration for navigation
ideas.tradeoffs: Adds ~8KB dependency (react-window), slightly more complex grid layout logic, requires fixed item heights

ideas.title: Cache Image objects in BannerCanvas to prevent reloading
ideas.description: BannerCanvas creates new Image() objects on every render for both background and element images. This triggers redundant image decoding even when the source URLs haven't changed, causing visual flicker and CPU overhead.
ideas.rationale: The renderCanvas function creates `new Image()` instances for background and elements on every call. Even with browser caching, each new Image instance triggers decoding overhead. The canvas re-renders frequently during drag/resize operations, multiplying the impact.
ideas.currentMetric: New Image() creation on every canvas render (~30-60 times during a drag operation)
ideas.expectedImprovement: Eliminate redundant image loading/decoding, smoother drag/resize interactions, ~20% faster canvas updates
ideas.implementation:
1. Create a useRef-based image cache Map<string, HTMLImageElement>
2. Check cache before creating new Image instances
3. Preload images when URLs change using useEffect
4. Use onload callbacks to trigger re-render only when image is ready
5. Implement cache eviction for removed images
ideas.tradeoffs: Slightly more memory usage for cached images, need to handle cache invalidation when images change

ideas.title: Memoize keyboard shortcut handlers in App.tsx
ideas.description: The `getDefaultShortcuts()` function is called on every App render, creating new function objects for all shortcut handlers. These new references cause the useKeyboardShortcuts hook to re-register event listeners unnecessarily.
ideas.rationale: App.tsx calls getDefaultShortcuts() with inline arrow functions on every render. This creates new function references that fail React's referential equality checks, potentially causing unnecessary effect re-runs and memory churn.
ideas.currentMetric: New shortcut handler objects created on every App render
ideas.expectedImprovement: Stable function references, fewer effect re-runs, reduced memory allocation during interaction
ideas.implementation:
1. Wrap the getDefaultShortcuts call with useMemo
2. Use useCallback for individual handlers passed to getDefaultShortcuts
3. Add proper dependency arrays referencing only truly dynamic values
4. Consider moving shortcut definitions outside component if possible
ideas.tradeoffs: Slight increase in code complexity with additional memoization hooks

ideas.title: Add request deduplication for concurrent API calls
ideas.description: The LLM service doesn't deduplicate identical concurrent requests. When users rapidly click generate or the voice agent fires multiple similar requests, duplicate API calls are made, wasting credits and bandwidth.
ideas.rationale: Without request deduplication, double-clicking 'Generate' or rapid voice commands can trigger multiple expensive AI API calls with identical parameters. This wastes user credits ($0.03-$0.24 per call) and creates race conditions in the UI.
ideas.currentMetric: No protection against duplicate concurrent requests
ideas.expectedImprovement: Prevent duplicate API calls, save user credits, cleaner UI state management, ~50% reduction in accidental duplicate requests
ideas.implementation:
1. Create a request deduplication layer in api.ts
2. Hash request parameters to create unique keys
3. Return existing promise for in-flight identical requests
4. Implement configurable TTL for request deduplication (e.g., 2 seconds)
5. Add optional override for intentional duplicate requests
ideas.tradeoffs: Slightly more complex request handling, need to handle edge cases for intentionally repeated requests

ideas.title: Split llm.ts into domain-specific service modules
ideas.description: The file src/services/llm.ts has grown to 790 lines and handles multiple unrelated concerns: chat completions (design, agent, search, thinking), image generation, prompt enhancement, image editing/analysis, and agent workflow orchestration. This violates single responsibility and makes the file difficult to navigate.
ideas.rationale: Large files with mixed responsibilities increase cognitive load, make testing harder, cause merge conflicts, and reduce code discoverability. Splitting into focused modules enables better separation of concerns, easier testing, and clearer API boundaries.
ideas.currentState: Single 790-line file handling: chat completions (5 functions), image generation (1 complex function with fallback chain), image operations (7 functions: edit, analyze, remove bg, upscale, outpaint, restore, analyze canvas), prompt enhancement, and agent workflow functions
ideas.proposedChange:
Split into focused service modules:
- src/services/ai/chat.ts - Chat completion functions (generateDesignChatResponse, generateAgentResponse, etc.)
- src/services/ai/imageGeneration.ts - Image generation with fallback chain
- src/services/ai/imageOperations.ts - Image editing, analysis, upscale, restore, remove bg
- src/services/ai/promptEnhancement.ts - Prompt enhancement logic
- src/services/ai/agentWorkflows.ts - Agent-based workflow orchestration (generateWithAgents)
- src/services/ai/index.ts - Barrel export for backward compatibility
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change. AI chat, image generation, and image processing are distinct domains that evolve independently.
prerequisites: Ensure comprehensive test coverage for llm.ts before refactoring
Update all import statements via search-replace

ideas.title: Refactor actionExecutor.ts giant switch statement using command pattern
ideas.description: The ActionExecutor class in src/services/actionExecutor.ts contains a 90-line switch statement in executeToolCall() that handles 17 different tool types. This violates open/closed principle - adding new tools requires modifying the switch statement, increasing risk of bugs.
ideas.rationale: Giant switch statements are a code smell indicating missing polymorphism. The command pattern allows adding new tools without modifying existing code, improves testability of individual tools, and makes the codebase more maintainable.
ideas.currentState: 797-line file with a massive switch statement handling: generate_background, magic_edit, remove_background, upscale_image, restore_image, enhance_face, suggest_prompts, write_enhanced_prompt, add_text_element, update_element, delete_element, list_elements, navigate_to_tab, undo_action, redo_action, analyze_image, analyze_banner
ideas.proposedChange:
Refactor using command pattern:
1. Create a ToolHandler interface: { name: string; execute: (args) => Promise<ActionResult> }
2. Create individual handler classes or functions for each tool
3. Use a registry Map<string, ToolHandler> instead of switch
4. Move tool handlers to src/services/actionExecutor/handlers/*.ts
ideas.bestPractice: Open/Closed Principle & Command Pattern - Classes should be open for extension but closed for modification. New tools can be added without changing existing code.
prerequisites: Ensure actionExecutor.test.ts covers all 17 tool types before refactoring

ideas.title: Extract ChatInterface.tsx into smaller focused components
ideas.description: ChatInterface.tsx at 791 lines combines too many responsibilities: chat UI rendering, message state management, conversation persistence, tool execution handling, file attachment processing, and API key validation. The component has 15+ useState hooks indicating excessive state coupling.
ideas.rationale: Large React components are harder to test, maintain, and reuse. Extracting focused sub-components improves code organization, enables component-level testing, and makes the codebase easier to understand for new developers.
ideas.currentState:
791-line monolithic component with:
- 15+ useState hooks (input, attachedImages, mode, loading, processingFiles, etc.)
- Inline message rendering logic
- File upload handling
- Conversation persistence logic
- Tool execution callbacks
- Mode switching (design/search)
ideas.proposedChange:
Extract into focused components:
- src/components/chat/ChatContainer.tsx - Main container with message list
- src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx - Input field with file upload
- src/components/chat/ChatMessage.tsx - Individual message rendering
- src/components/chat/ChatModeToggle.tsx - Design/Search mode switcher
- src/components/chat/ConversationList.tsx - History sidebar
- src/hooks/useChatPersistence.ts - Extract persistence logic as custom hook
- src/hooks/useChatToolExecution.ts - Extract tool execution as custom hook
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle for React components. Extract custom hooks for complex state logic. Keep components under 200-300 lines for maintainability.
prerequisites: Add comprehensive tests for current ChatInterface behavior

ideas.title: Extract reusable urlToDataUri helper to shared utilities
ideas.description: The urlToDataUri helper function in ImageToolsPanel.tsx (lines 21-55) handles URL-to-base64 conversion with CORS fallback logic. This utility is likely needed in multiple places for image processing but is currently embedded in a component file.
ideas.rationale: Utility functions embedded in component files reduce discoverability and lead to duplication. Moving to a shared utility enables reuse, centralized testing, and consistent behavior across the codebase.
ideas.currentState:
35-line urlToDataUri function in ImageToolsPanel.tsx handles:
- Data URI passthrough
- External URL CORS fetch with blob conversion
- Relative URL fetch with blob conversion
- Error fallback returning original URL
ideas.proposedChange:
Move urlToDataUri to src/utils/imageUtils.ts (already exists) alongside related image utilities. Export it for use across components that process images:
- ImageToolsPanel.tsx
- Any future components needing image data URI conversion
- Potential use in services/replicate.ts
ideas.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - Extract common logic into reusable utilities. Keep component files focused on rendering logic.
prerequisites: Add unit tests for urlToDataUri covering all edge cases (data URI, CORS success, CORS failure, relative URL)

ideas.title: Add missing test coverage for critical service modules
ideas.description: While 21 test files exist, several critical services lack dedicated tests or have minimal coverage. Key services like apiKeyStorage.ts, brandEngine.ts, chatPersistence.ts, liveClient.ts, and modelRouter.ts have no corresponding test files despite handling sensitive data and core business logic.
ideas.rationale: Critical services handling authentication, API keys, and AI model routing need comprehensive test coverage to prevent regressions. Testing these services ensures reliability and makes refactoring safer.

21 test files exist covering:
- Core contexts (AIContext, AuthContext, CanvasContext)
- Key services (replicate, openrouter, actionExecutor, auth, llm, database)
